big_question: Whose money is entering the system?
current_best_evidence: Private-credit AUM/deployment rows; insurance and retirement balance-sheet rows; bank denominator rows; utility/customer tariff evidence.
what_is_still_missing: Consistent source taxonomy across banks private credit insurers public bonds equity customer prepayments ratepayers government grants and project sponsors.
why_it_matters: Without source separation we cannot say whether capital is new money bank replacement customer-funded project money or balance-sheet recycling.

current_best_evidence: Credit agreements and debt stacks for ET Cheniere URI Sterling; BDC holder schedules; utility dockets; ABL/securitization first-pass rows.
what_is_still_missing: Standard vehicle classes across all companies: corporate debt project/entity debt ABL AR securitization revolver L/C surety private credit insurance SMA regulated recovery equity and customer advances.
why_it_matters: The wrapper tells us what the market thinks can be pledged recovered contracted or flexibly supported.

big_question: Which companies actually receive or route capital?
current_best_evidence: 519-company triage; 71 lane candidates; named borrower crosswalks; ET Cheniere URI Sterling source-table passes.
what_is_still_missing: A normalized company universe that assigns every company to one or more capital-flow roles: source router vehicle borrower owner operator supplier contractor or regulator-recovery platform.
why_it_matters: Without roles the analysis becomes a list of interesting companies instead of a capital-flow map.

current_best_evidence: DOE LNG cargo rows; EIA export denominators; URI fleet OEC and capex; Sterling backlog/RPO rows; AEP/Duke tariff/docket evidence.
what_is_still_missing: Project-level or asset-level identity for power load generation grid upgrades LNG trains pipelines fleet categories data centers public works and customer sites.
why_it_matters: This is the difference between a theme and a real economic destination.

current_best_evidence: Some debt proceeds and refinancing language; Cheniere equity-funded growth-capex split; Sterling use-of-proceeds agreement terms; borrower transaction clues.
what_is_still_missing: Separate acquisition financing refinancing capex working capital dividends rescue capital project construction debt repayment and L/C/surety support.
why_it_matters: A dollar used to refinance old debt means something different from a dollar that builds new capacity.

current_best_evidence: Cheniere reported cargoes matched DOE vessel rows; URI fleet capex-to-cash bridge; Sterling backlog/cash bridge; utility load/docket paths.
what_is_still_missing: Repeatable conversion metrics: MW in service cargoes volumes fleet OEC utilization backlog burn RPO conversion revenue margin OCF FCF and rate-base growth.
why_it_matters: Capital flow only matters if it becomes operating capacity cash flow or control.

big_question: Who earns cash and what return/risk is visible?
current_best_evidence: Operating cash flow and capex rows for ET Cheniere URI Sterling; insurer spread earnings; asset-manager fee/AUM rows.
what_is_still_missing: Margin returns interest cost fee economics spread earnings project economics customer payments and covenant/rating effects.
why_it_matters: This decides whether capital is profitable productive risky or only gross activity.

big_question: Is the evidence a trend or a point-in-time snapshot?
current_best_evidence: Annual/Q2 baselines for capital-intensive companies; some multi-period private-credit and insurance metrics; Sterling next eight-quarter queue.
what_is_still_missing: Eight-quarter or multi-year series for each critical metric by lane and company.
why_it_matters: A one-quarter spike can mislead; durable capital flow needs time-series proof.

big_question: Is the company evidence large relative to the market?
current_best_evidence: FRED bank denominators; EIA/DOE LNG/NGL denominators; Census construction/data-center denominators; project denominator workbench.
what_is_still_missing: Consistent outside denominators by lane: bank credit private credit direct lending utility load construction spending LNG export capacity fleet markets and public funding.
why_it_matters: Outside denominators prevent overclaiming company anecdotes as macro trends.

big_question: What would make the thesis wrong?
current_best_evidence: Claim dashboard and funding-type hypothesis map include disproof tests; Sterling rows explicitly mark missing L/C usage and project-source proof.
what_is_still_missing: Hard disproof triggers by lane: bank credit still growing in same lane backlog not funded projects cancelled capex maintenance-only poor cash conversion weak utilization and low-margin acquired backlog.
why_it_matters: The system should learn from contradiction rather than collect confirming evidence only.

big_question: What can we safely say today?
current_best_evidence: Cross-theme dashboard; evidence ledger; claim strength scorecard; status buckets from queued to thesis-grade.
what_is_still_missing: One promoted-claim table and one forbidden-overclaim table across all themes and companies.
why_it_matters: This keeps writing honest and stops hypotheses from becoming conclusions too early.

big_question: How do we extend beyond the first examples?
current_best_evidence: 519-company triage and all-company scale-up operating model exist; first detailed passes focus on selected lanes.
what_is_still_missing: A repeatable extraction template for all 511-plus companies by sector and theme, with prioritization rules and minimum fields.
why_it_matters: The long-run goal is a mapped operating system, not a handful of case studies.
